title: India court orders release of 'Cockroach' movement leaders

'Cockroach' leaders ordered released from detention, party says
An executive court in Delhi has ordered the release of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke and other leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, the youth-led movement said on Sunday.
The three were detained ahead of a large protest in Dehli on Saturday and appeared in court earlier on Sunday after being in detention for nearly 24 hours.
Earlier, the CJP had alleged the leaders were being detained at an undisclosed location and did not have access to their lawyers.
On Saturday evening, the CJP issued a fresh call for a march to New Delhi's Jantar Mantar on Sunday.
"We're not backing down! We will march to Jantar Mantar again tomorrow," Ajinkya Shinde, the CJP's interim protest leader, said at a press conference.
The exact number of demonstrators detained during the protest could not be immediately verified.
Shinde told reporters that over 15,000 people, including students, had been detained across India.
The Hindu newspaper, citing Delhi Police sources, reported that 2,500 demonstrators were detained in Delhi on top of 1,000 people picked up in overnight preventive measures ahead of the protest.
Indian media reports cite Delhi Police as saying that all detainees had been released later on Saturday.
